'''Lee-Jen Wei''' ({{lang-zh|c=魏立人}}) is a Taiwanese-American [[biostatistician]] who is a professor of biostatistics at [[Harvard University]].

==Education==
Wei graduated from [[Fu Jen Catholic University]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in mathematics  in 1970.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.frontierscience.org/docs/CV-lee-jen-wei.pdf | title=Curriculum Vitae - LJ Wei | access-date=2024-06-23 | website=www.frontierscience.org}}</ref> He then earned his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Wisconsin&ndash;Madison]] in 1975.<ref name="Harvard15">{{cite web|url=http://www.hsph.harvard.edu/faculty/l-wei/|title=Lee-Jen Wei|publisher=Harvard School of Public Health|accessdate=2011-11-05}}</ref> 

== Academic career ==
Before joining the faculty of  [[Harvard University]], he was a tenured Professor of Biostatistics and Statistics at the [[University of South Carolina]], [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], the [[University of Michigan]], and the [[George Washington University]] from 1982 to 1991.<ref name="Harvard15" /> He was named Cancer Expert by The [[National Cancer Institute]] in 1980.<ref name="Harvard15" />

He has been a tenured Professor of Biostatistics at Harvard University since 1991 and was the co-director of the Bioinformatics Core at the Harvard School of Public Health from 2003 to 2007.<ref name="Harvard15" /> From 2003 to 2004, he served as the acting chair of the Department of Biostatistics at Harvard University.<ref name="Harvard15" /> Under his supervision, the department successfully converted the doctor of science degree program in biostatistics (a professional degree) to a conventional (art and sciences) Ph.D. program at the Harvard Graduate School.<ref name="Harvard15" /> This was an important accomplishment since the department had tried this conversion for more than 20 years without success.<ref name="Harvard15" />

==Research and contributions==
Wei has developed and published a number of novel quantitative methods for analyzing data from experimental and observational studies.<ref name="Harvard15"/> Specifically, he has published many papers on monitoring drug and device safety and related topics.<ref name="Harvard15"/> The resulting procedures have been utilized for various drug and device regulatory evaluations involving safety issues.  His extensive experience in quantitative science for making inferences about the drug and device safety is readily applicable to the general industry product safety issues.<ref name="Harvard15"/>

Wei has also served on numerous Data Safety Monitoring Boards for experimental studies for the drug industry.<ref name="Harvard15"/> And has moreover been intimately involved in designing, monitoring and analyzing various kinds of studies in assessing [[postmarketing surveillance]] data to identify signals of safety concerns.<ref name="Harvard15"/>

Wei's scholarly writings include over 130 articles in peer-reviewed academic journals.<ref name="Harvard15"/> He is responsible for developing numerous novel statistical methods for practitioners.<ref name="Harvard15"/> Many of these methods have been included in the most commonly used statistical packages such as SAS, S-plus, and R.<ref name="Harvard15"/> He has additionally served on the editorial boards of a number of statistical journals and am an elected Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] and [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].<ref name="Harvard15"/>

==Awards and recognition==
In 1986 he was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm View/Search Fellows of the ASA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/https://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |date=2016-06-16 }}, accessed 2016-10-29.</ref>

In 1999 he was awarded the Outstanding Alumni Award of [[Fu Jen Catholic University]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.pro.fju.edu.tw/alumni06-1.asp |title=輔仁大學歷屆傑出校友一覽 |access-date=2018-07-23 |archive-date=2018-07-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180709214129/http://www.pro.fju.edu.tw/alumni06-1.asp |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Professor Wei was named “Statistician of the Year” in 2007 by the Boston Chapter of the American Statistical Association.<ref name="Harvard15"/>

The [[American Statistical Association]] gave him the [[Wilks Memorial Award]] in 2009 "for statistical methods used in clinical trials",<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.amstat.org/awards/samuelwilksaward.cfm| title=Wilks Memorial Award| accessdate=2011-11-05| publisher=American Statistical Association| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130627075200/http://amstat.org/awards/samuelwilksaward.cfm| archive-date=2013-06-27| url-status=dead}}</ref> which is one of the most prestigious awards among all the international statistical societies.
